mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as capital flows into equities.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 8.0% in the prior month signals economic distress and triggers risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand, causing equity market sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS are below 470 and 347000 respectively, the S&P 500 generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (INDPRO growth > 0.5% monthly), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an imminent economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in INDPRO does not produce negative 20-day returns (e.g., returns are positive in > 60% of such instances).

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) above 450 thousand units signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 450, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.0% signals potential monetary tightening, causing equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL yoy change exceeds 2.0%, the S&P 500 generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where PAYEMS exceeds 133000 and UNRATE is below 8.2%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime (INDPRO growth > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%), rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals sustained economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-shock recovery regime, a rising INDPRO does not produce positive 5-day returns (e.g., returns are negative in > 60% of such instances).
